title: Cut a cable tie off a cable bundle without nicking the cables
instruction: Cut the cable tie off the cable bundle with the flush cutters from the tray, without nicking any cable's insulation. Then put the cutters back on the tray's rests, leave the bundle across its blocks with nothing holding it, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Technicians cut cable ties off wiring looms, harnesses and network bundles every day. A careless snip nicks the insulation, which can later short or shock someone. The safe way is to hold the bundle still and cut the strap right beside the tie's head, where it stands off the cables.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. Two beech blocks (6 x 5 cm, 5 cm tall) stand 30 cm forward, one 12 cm left and one 16 cm right of the centre line. Across them lies a bundle of seven PVC-insulated copper cables (7 mm each, coloured; 2.1 cm across, 38 cm long, 120 g), running left to right. A black nylon cable tie (4 mm wide strap) is round the bundle 4 cm right of the centre line, between the blocks, its head (7 x 6 x 6 mm) on the near side of the bundle, 30 degrees up from level; the strap lies on the six outer cables and bridges the grooves between them. A grey ABS tray (18 x 10 cm, 2.5 cm walls) lies 16 cm forward and 25 cm right of the centre line, with two dark rubber rests across it. On the rests lie flush cutters with steel jaws and red PVC-sleeved handles, their jaws pointing forward. The cutters are two steel halves on a pivot (60 g each, 13.4 cm long); the handles are 2.9 cm apart where a hand holds them, 5 cm behind the pivot (about 3.5 cm above the table), and a spring holds the jaws 8 mm open at the tips. Squeezing the handles together closes the jaws; closed 10 degrees, they cut whatever is between the tips. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. The real-world score: the cut counts when the tie's strap is physically cut through and the tie has come off the bundle (no longer round any cable), wherever along the strap it was cut; afterwards every cable's insulation is inspected all round under a 10x magnifier, and any nick, cut or crush mark scores 0. Simulation proxies for those two judgements (the simulation's score, not the real-world one): severed: the jaws close (10 degrees) with the strap truly between the blades, anywhere along it: the strap's middle within 3 mm of the mouth's middle line (so all 4 mm of its width lies between the 8 mm-apart edges), the jaws' tips no more than 10.9 mm from the bundle's axis (at or past the strap's inner face, 10.5 mm from it), the cutters pointing into the bundle (within 50 degrees) and their pivot axis within 50 degrees of the strap's run; the cut tie then falls off. Off the bundle: the cut tie's middle at least 1.5 cm below the bundle's axis or 3 cm from it. Nicked: the strap cut where it lies on a cable (less than 0.5 mm between its inner face and the insulation where the jaws' middle closes on it, so the blades close on that cable), or the jaws closing at any time with a jaw pressed 0.5 mm or more into a cable. A clean cut is possible over any of the six grooves between the outer cables, including just below the head. Tiers: 0.0 if a cable was nicked. Otherwise 1.0: the tie severed and off the bundle, both halves of the cutters back on the tray's rests (within 3 cm of where they lay), the bundle still across its blocks (its middle within 2.5 cm of its line and not below the blocks' tops), each gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) at least 4 cm from the cutters' handles and from the bundle above its left block, and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the tie severed and off the bundle; 0.25: the cutters lifted 2 cm out of the tray at some point; else 0.0. In a real trial the end state is measured with a ruler against marks on the tray and the blocks and from the robot's joint log, and the 0.25 tier from the overhead video. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the cutters and the bundle still.
reset_notes: Put a new tie round the bundle at the same place, its head on the near side, lay the bundle back across the blocks and the cutters back in the tray.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the bundle is one rigid body with the tie glued to it; its strap lies on the outer cables and bridges the grooves between them (a real strap also stands off beside its head). Cut and nick are simulation proxies: when the jaws close with the strap between the blades, the tie is swapped for an open one that falls off; a nick is judged from the gap under the strap and how deep a jaw pressed. Real trials inspect tie and cables.
